steps.name: limma-voom differential expression, case vs control
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 60 cases and 60 controls, using a method whose false discovery rate is trustworthy at this sample size?

grounding.reason: Population-scale cohort (n=60/group): limma-voom fixed-effects model is primary per R-0015 warn flag; Wilcoxon control stated as required caution; apeglm shrinkage per R-0009 for reporting only.

steps.description: Fit voom on the filtered, TMM-normalized counts with design ~condition (reference level explicitly set to 'control', contrast named condition case-vs-control), then lmFit and eBayes (limma-voom fixed-effects linear model). Because each group holds 60 samples (>=50), a count-based GLM (DESeq2/edgeR) would inflate false positives on this kind of population cohort per the knowledge base, so limma-voom is the primary test; additionally run a Wilcoxon rank-sum test per gene on the log-CPM values as a nonparametric control and report the overlap between the two gene lists. Also run apeglm-based log2FC shrinkage via a parallel DESeq2 fit (single coefficient) purely for reporting shrunken effect sizes and MA/dispersion diagnostic plots, not for the primary test.
acceptance_criteria: limma-voom model fit with explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (case vs control)

steps.name: Case-vs-control classifier: nested cross-validated penalized logistic regression
steps.question: Can a gene-expression classifier distinguish a case from a control sample, and how accurately would it perform on a new, unseen sample?

grounding.reason: Classifier of sample class from expression: penalized logistic regression (glmnet) with nested CV and ROC/AUC with CI, feature selection inside each fold, per R-0155; DE-derived feature list explicitly not reused per translational-considerations rule on optimistic bias.

steps.description: On the filtered, TMM-normalized, voom-transformed log-CPM matrix (120 samples x filtered genes from T1S2), fit a penalized (elastic-net/lasso) logistic regression with glmnet to classify case vs control. Use nested cross-validation: an outer loop (e.g. 10-fold, repeated) to obtain an honest out-of-fold performance estimate, and an inner loop within each outer training fold to select the regularization parameter lambda by cross-validated deviance. Critically, do NOT reuse the T1S3/T1S4 DE gene list as a fixed feature set for the classifier — refit the gene filtering, scaling/centering, and glmnet feature selection independently inside each outer training fold, so that no information from a held-out fold's samples leaks into its own prediction. Report the outer-fold ROC curve, AUC with a confidence interval (pROC), and the genes with nonzero coefficients per fold, explicitly noting instability of the selected gene set across folds given the class sizes. State plainly that this cross-validated AUC is the estimate of accuracy on a new sample, and that it would be optimistic if the DE feature list from T1S3/T1S4 were used instead.
acceptance_criteria: Feature selection, scaling, and glmnet lambda selection performed independently inside each outer training fold (no leakage from DE step or from held-out samples)
Nested cross-validation performed: inner loop tunes lambda, outer loop yields out-of-fold predictions
ROC curve and AUC with 95% CI reported from pooled out-of-fold predictions

Explicit statement that this AUC is the answer to 'how accurate on a new sample', distinct from and not reusing the population-level DE gene list as a preselected feature set

plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE + classifier (n=120)
plan.analytical_narrative: 120 whole-blood bulk RNA-seq samples (60 cases, 60 controls, single batch, unpaired) from Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 121 columns incl. gene symbol) are used to (1) characterize what separates cases from controls at the gene and pathway level, and (2) build and honestly evaluate a classifier that predicts case/control status on a new sample. Because each group holds >=50 samples, the knowledge base flags that DESeq2/edgeR's negative-binomial assumption is violated in population-scale cohorts (inflated false positives even on permuted labels), so the differential expression test uses limma-voom with TMM normalization instead of a count-based GLM, with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test run alongside as a nonparametric control. Enrichment runs camera directly on the limma fit (accounts for inter-gene correlation, valid at this sample size) against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, all present in the reference store for human. For the classifier, the DE gene list from the population-level contrast is NOT reused as a fixed feature set for prediction (that would be train/test leakage via double-dipping); instead a penalized logistic regression (glmnet) with nested cross-validation performs feature selection and hyperparameter tuning inside each training fold, and out-of-fold predictions give an honest ROC/AUC with a confidence interval as the answer to 'how accurate on a new sample'. Every step is grounded in the returned procedure (rules R-0002/0009/0010/0015/0026/0029/0033/0036/0037/0038/0043/0045/0046/0047/0048/0054/0057/0058/0083/0088/0098/0099/0101/0103/0107/0108/0155/0165, snapshot sha256:90c687582244894c67c212e63855415984027bcd54c896821c4e065cf8b5467a), validated with execute_knowledge_check (ok:true after correcting the multiple-testing step name).
